sources.standing: active individual Internet-Draft; not endorsed by the IETF and no formal standing in the IETF standards process

review_triggers: a new AAT revision is published
an independent draft-01 implementation fixture becomes available
decision.draft_01_handling: accept only with the exact Ardur DG v0.2 profile identifier; reject unprofiled, mixed, unknown, and cross-version wire forms

changes.draft_00: Section 3.1 defines delegation and execution token types through required aat_type values; only an execution leaf may invoke a tool.
changes.draft_01: Section 3.1 removes separate token types; root, intermediate, and leaf roles are determined only by chain position.
changes.security_impact: A draft-01 token omits a claim required by draft-00, and a draft-01 verifier must not infer the old structural planning/invocation boundary.
changes.ardur_disposition: Keep aat_type mandatory in DG v0.1 and reject its absence as unsupported draft-01 wire semantics.

changes.draft_00: Section 3.2 registers aat_type as a required common claim.
changes.draft_01: Section 3.2 removes aat_type from the common-claim table; jti, iss, iat, exp, cnf, del_depth, del_max_depth, par_hash, and authorization_details remain.
changes.security_impact: Unknown top-level claims are ignored, so a generic draft-01 verifier could accept a draft-00 token unless a deployment profile enforces revision separation.
changes.ardur_disposition: Use required aat_type presence as the unambiguous v0.1 compatibility discriminator.

changes.draft_00: The PoP JWT has jti, iat, aat_id, aat_tool, and hta.
changes.draft_01: Section 5.2 adds optional aat_aud; profiles that require audience binding must require and verify it.
changes.security_impact: Audience-free PoP can be replayed at another enforcement point within its time window when keys and tool identifiers overlap.
changes.ardur_disposition: Do not add aat_aud to DG v0.1. Require an explicit v0.2 profile decision before enabling audience-bound draft-01 PoP.

changes.draft_00: Section 3.4 defines exact, pattern, range, one_of, not_one_of, contains, subset, regex, cel, wildcard, all, any, and not as core constraints.
changes.draft_01: Section 3.4 retains exact, range, one_of, not_one_of, contains, subset, wildcard, all, and any; pattern, regex, cel, and not require separately registered extension semantics.
changes.security_impact: Treating removed constraints as draft-01 core constraints would overstate interoperability and could apply non-portable matching or subsumption rules.
changes.ardur_disposition: Keep the draft-00 registry for DG v0.1. A draft-01 migration must version or reject every removed constraint before processing the chain.

changes.draft_00: Section 6 selects child aat_type and requires a fresh holder key when the type changes; same-scope derivation is valid but discouraged.
changes.draft_01: Section 6 removes type selection and the type-transition key rule; same-scope derivation may support holder-key handoff or subprocess delegation.
changes.security_impact: The old structural key boundary cannot be carried forward as if it were a draft-01 invariant.
changes.ardur_disposition: Preserve draft-00 type-transition checks in DG v0.1. Define any draft-01 role/key policy as a versioned Ardur profile extension.

changes.draft_00: Section 6 requires temporal attenuation, while Section 4.4 states child iat must not precede parent iat.
changes.draft_01: Section 6 makes the child iat >= parent iat requirement explicit in the derivation procedure and keeps expiration bounded by the parent.
changes.security_impact: This is a clarification that prevents backdated child grants.
changes.ardur_disposition: Retain and test the existing monotonic iat/exp checks.

changes.draft_00: Section 7 validates aat_type on every token, enforces type-transition key separation, and denies a delegation leaf.
changes.draft_01: Section 7 removes type checks and authorizes only the chain-position leaf after full chain and PoP verification.
changes.security_impact: Mixing algorithms would either reject valid draft-01 chains or silently remove draft-00 invocation-boundary checks.
changes.ardur_disposition: Keep the draft-00 algorithm intact and return an explicit unsupported-revision error when aat_type is absent.

changes.draft_00: Root and child required-claim checks leave some public-key and single-token-chain requirements implicit or inconsistently worded.
changes.draft_01: Section 7 explicitly rejects private JWK parameters, requires exactly one root AAT authorization entry, and closes the single-token-chain validation bypass.
changes.security_impact: Accepting private key material leaks holder secrets; weak single-token validation can bypass checks normally performed on adjacent links.
changes.ardur_disposition: Backport the fail-closed public-key and required-claim checks where they do not change valid DG v0.1 wire semantics.

changes.draft_00: Ed25519 support is mandatory; every token and PoP algorithm must be allowlisted, key-compatible, and asymmetric.
changes.draft_01: The Ed25519 support requirement and per-token asymmetric algorithm allowlist remain; section numbering moves from 8.14 to 8.13.
changes.security_impact: Algorithm confusion remains a chain-wide risk at every signature boundary.
changes.ardur_disposition: Keep the current EdDSA-only Go profile as a strict subset and retain per-token allowlisting.

changes.draft_00: Section 8.12 makes type-transition key separation a protocol invariant and Section 8.13 carries CEL-specific privilege-escalation rules.
changes.draft_01: Section 8.12 makes role-based key separation deployment guidance, removes CEL-specific core rules, and adds Section 8.10 guidance for profile-defined approval gates.
changes.security_impact: Planning/invocation separation and approval preservation become profile responsibilities instead of base-protocol guarantees.
changes.ardur_disposition: Do not claim draft-01 security semantics until a versioned profile defines role keys, approvals, and removed-constraint handling.

changes.draft_00: Section 8.15 states that signed token contents are visible and recommends encrypted transport and sensitive storage.
changes.draft_01: The dedicated section is removed, while the tokens remain signed rather than encrypted.
changes.security_impact: Removing the section does not remove the confidentiality risk.
changes.ardur_disposition: Retain the DG v0.1 TLS and sensitive-storage requirement as an Ardur security boundary.

changes.draft_00: Appendix D is titled a normative CBOR/CWT profile but defers claim keys, COSE rules, and an interoperable profile to a companion draft.
changes.draft_01: Appendix D is explicitly non-normative and states that JWT/JWS is the only fully specified encoding.
changes.security_impact: Claiming unchanged CWT interoperability would be unsupported by either complete wire assignments or independent fixtures.
changes.ardur_disposition: DG v0.1 support is JWT/JWS only; remove the prior statement that the profile applies unchanged to CWT.
